question: Which river basin originates from the Western Ghats range of Karnataka state and has many tributaries such as the Noyyal, Kabini, Arkavathi and Amaravati?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kaveri.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Kaveri (Cauvery) river originates at Talakaveri in the Brahmagiri range of the Western Ghats, Kodagu (Coorg) district, Karnataka, and flows south-eastward through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu into the Bay of Bengal. (कावेरी नदी — पश्चिमी घाट, कर्नाटक)

 

• Its major tributaries include the Kabini, Bhavani, Arkavathi, Noyyal, Amaravati, Hemavati and Lakshmana Tirtha, several of which join it after rising in the Western Ghats/Nilgiris.

 

• The Kaveri basin is one of the major river basins of peninsular India and is often called the "Ganga of the South" (Dakshin Ganga).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kaveri is the subject of the long-standing Cauvery water dispute between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, adjudicated by the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal.

 

• An important waterfall on the Kaveri is the Shivanasamudra Falls in Karnataka.

 

NOTE

 

• Sabarmati (Option 1): Rises near Udaipur in the Aravalli Range, Rajasthan, and flows through Gujarat into the Gulf of Khambhat.

 

• Brahmani (Option 2): Formed by the confluence of the Sankh and South Koel rivers in Odisha; it is not a Western Ghats river.

 

• Periyar (Option 4): Kerala's largest river by discharge, originates in the Western Ghats but its tributaries are the Muthirapuzha, Mullayar, etc., not Noyyal/Kabini/Arkavathi.

question: Which s-block element is a silvery-white metal that is used in an alloy with copper or nickel to make gyroscopes, springs, electrical contacts, spot-welding electrodes, and non-sparking equipment?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Beryllium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Beryllium (Be, atomic number 4) is a hard, silvery-white alkaline earth (s-block) metal. Alloyed with copper (beryllium copper) or nickel, it gives high strength, corrosion resistance and non-sparking properties. (बेरिलियम — s-ब्लॉक तत्व)

 

• Beryllium-copper alloys are used to make gyroscopes, springs, electrical/electronic contacts, spot-welding electrodes and non-sparking tools used in oil rigs and mines where a spark could ignite flammable gases.

 

• Beryllium belongs to Group 2 (alkaline earth metals) of the periodic table, along with magnesium, calcium, strontium, barium and radium.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Beryllium is also valued for its low density and high stiffness, making it useful in aerospace components and X-ray equipment windows.

 

• Emerald and aquamarine are gemstone varieties of the mineral beryl, from which beryllium is extracted.

 

NOTE

 

• Rubidium (Option 2): A soft, silvery alkali metal (Group 1), highly reactive with water; not used for gyroscope/spring alloys.

 

• Francium (Option 3): An extremely rare, highly radioactive alkali metal; far too unstable for any structural or alloy use.

 

• Caesium (Option 4): A soft, gold-coloured alkali metal used in atomic clocks and photoelectric cells, not in copper/nickel non-sparking alloys.

question: Who among the following personalities was appointed as the legal advisor of the Constituent Assembly that drafted the document of the Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is BN Rau.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sir Benegal Narsing Rau (B.N. Rau) was appointed the Constitutional Advisor (legal advisor) to the Constituent Assembly of India and prepared the original draft of the Constitution, which was then examined by the Drafting Committee. (बी.एन. राव — संविधान सलाहकार)

 

• B.N. Rau studied the constitutions of several countries and drew up an initial draft in 1947-48, which formed the basis for the Drafting Committee's work.

 

• The Drafting Committee, chaired by Dr B.R. Ambedkar, refined Rau's draft into the final Constitution, adopted on 26 November 1949.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• B.N. Rau later served as India's representative to the UN Security Council and as a judge of the International Court of Justice.

 

• The Constituent Assembly had Dr Rajendra Prasad as its President.

 

NOTE

 

• HVR Iyengar (Option 1): Served as Secretary to the Constituent Assembly, an administrative (not legal advisory) role; he later became RBI Governor.

 

• SN Mukherjee (Option 2): Was the Chief Draftsman of the Constituent Assembly, responsible for the final language and wording of the Constitution.

 

• BR Ambedkar (Option 3): Chaired the Drafting Committee that used B.N. Rau's draft as its basis; he was not the Assembly's legal/constitutional advisor.

question: India won their first women's under-19 T20 Cricket World Cup 2023 by defeating:
solution_text:
The correct answer is England.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India won the inaugural ICC Women's U19 T20 World Cup 2023, held in South Africa, by defeating England in the final at Senwes Park, Potchefstroom, on 29 January 2023. (महिला अंडर-19 टी20 विश्व कप 2023 — भारत विजेता)

 

• Chasing a modest England total, India completed the win comfortably by 7 wickets, with Shafali Verma as India's captain.

 

• India had earlier beaten New Zealand in the semi-final to reach the final.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• This was the first-ever ICC Women's U19 World Cup, and India became its inaugural champion.

 

• India has also won the (men's) U19 Cricket World Cup on multiple occasions, most recently in 2022 under Yash Dhull.

 

NOTE

 

• Australia (Option 1): Did not reach the final of the 2023 Women's U19 T20 World Cup.

 

• South Africa (Option 2): Hosted the tournament but did not reach the final.

 

• Sri Lanka (Option 3): Did not reach the final of the 2023 Women's U19 T20 World Cup.

question: Which gas is the major component of biogas?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Methane.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Biogas is produced by the anaerobic digestion (bacterial decomposition in the absence of oxygen) of organic matter such as cattle dung, agricultural waste and sewage. Its major component is methane (CH₄), typically 50-70% by volume. (बायोगैस — मीथेन प्रमुख घटक)

 

• The remaining composition of biogas is mostly carbon dioxide (CO₂), with trace amounts of hydrogen sulphide, nitrogen, and moisture.

 

• Because of its high methane content, biogas is combustible and is used as fuel for cooking, lighting, and electricity generation, especially in rural gobar gas plants.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• CNG (Compressed Natural Gas), used as a vehicle fuel, is also predominantly methane but is a fossil-fuel-derived, compressed form of natural gas, distinct from biologically produced biogas.

 

• India promotes biogas production through schemes like the National Biogas and Manure Management Programme (NBMMP).

 

NOTE

 

• CNG (Option 1): A compressed, purified form of natural gas used as vehicle fuel; not the same as biogas, though also methane-rich.

 

• Hydrogen (Option 3): Not a significant component of biogas; explored separately as a clean fuel (green hydrogen).

 

• LPG (Option 4): A mixture of propane and butane derived from petroleum/natural gas processing, unrelated to biogas production.

question: What is the total route length of the Indian Railways (as of March 2020)?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 67,956 km.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per Ministry of Railways data, the total route length of Indian Railways stood at approximately 67,956 km as of March 2020, making it one of the largest railway networks in the world. (भारतीय रेलवे — मार्ग की लंबाई)

 

• Indian Railways operates on broad gauge (1,676 mm), metre gauge, and narrow gauge, with broad gauge accounting for the vast majority of the network.

 

• Indian Railways is organised into zones and divisions and is one of the world's largest employers.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Route length differs from total track length (running + siding kilometres), which is significantly higher than the route length figure.

 

• Indian Railways was established in 1853, when the first passenger train ran between Bombay (Mumbai) and Thane.

 

NOTE

 

• 63,950 km (Option 2): Does not match the officially reported route length as of March 2020.

 

• 91,604 km (Option 3): This figure considerably overstates the actual route length of Indian Railways.

 

• 82,402 km (Option 4): This figure also does not match the officially reported route length as of March 2020.

question: Mohiniyattam is a dance form of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kerala.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mohiniyattam ("dance of the enchantress") is one of the eight classical dance forms of India and is native to Kerala. (मोहिनीअट्टम — केरल)

 

• It is traditionally performed as a solo dance by women, characterised by graceful, swaying body movements, and draws on Hindu mythology, particularly the story of Lord Vishnu's Mohini avatar.

 

• Dancers wear a distinctive cream and gold-bordered (kasavu) sari, and the dance is accompanied by Carnatic music and the Malayalam language.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kerala is also home to the classical dance-drama Kathakali and the martial art Kalaripayattu.

 

• The eight classical dances of India are Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali & Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

 

NOTE

 

• West Bengal (Option 1): Known for folk forms like Chhau (Purulia) and Gaudiya Nritya, not Mohiniyattam.

 

• Tamil Nadu (Option 2): Home to the classical dance Bharatanatyam.

 

• Maharashtra (Option 3): Known for folk dances like Lavani and Koli, not Mohiniyattam.

question: Which music director is popularly known as ‘Pancham’?
solution_text:
The correct answer is R D Burman.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rahul Dev Burman (R.D. Burman), one of Hindi cinema's most influential music composers, was popularly nicknamed "Pancham" — a name reportedly given to him by actor Ashok Kumar. (आर.डी. बर्मन — 'पंचम')

 

• R.D. Burman was the son of noted composer S.D. Burman and composed music for hundreds of Hindi films from the 1960s to the 1990s, blending Indian and Western musical styles.

 

• He remains one of the most celebrated names in Indian film music, with his compositions still remixed and referenced widely.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• R.D. Burman's notable film scores include Sholay, Yaadon Ki Baaraat, Amar Prem and 1942: A Love Story (released posthumously).

 

• His father, S.D. Burman, was himself a legendary composer and singer of Hindi and Bengali music.

 

NOTE

 

• Khayyam (Option 1): Noted music director known for films like Umrao Jaan and Kabhi Kabhie, not nicknamed 'Pancham'.

 

• S D Burman (Option 2): R.D. Burman's father and himself an eminent composer, but not the one called 'Pancham'.

 

• Anu Malik (Option 4): A later-generation Bollywood music director, unrelated to the 'Pancham' nickname.

question: Based on the recommendations of which Committee was the creation of a separate category for NBFCs operating in the microfinance sector (NBFC-MFI) done?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Malegam Committee.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Malegam Committee, headed by Y.H. Malegam, was constituted by the RBI in 2010 to study issues in the microfinance sector following the Andhra Pradesh MFI crisis. (मालेगाम समिति — NBFC-MFI श्रेणी)

 

• Based on its recommendations (submitted in 2011), the RBI created a separate regulatory category, NBFC-MFI (Non-Banking Financial Company - Micro Finance Institution), with norms on interest rate caps, margin caps, and lending limits.

 

• The committee's recommendations aimed to protect borrowers from over-indebtedness and coercive recovery practices while ensuring the sector's orderly growth.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Narasimhan Committee (1991 and 1998) dealt with banking sector reforms, not microfinance regulation specifically.

 

• RBI has since revised NBFC-MFI regulations, including through a 2022 harmonised regulatory framework for microfinance loans.

 

NOTE

 

• Narasimhan Committee (Option 1): Focused on banking sector and financial sector reforms, not the creation of the NBFC-MFI category.

 

• Deepak Parekh Committee (Option 3): Deepak Parekh has headed various financial-sector panels, but not the one that created the NBFC-MFI category.

 

• PK Mohanty Committee (Option 4): Associated with matters such as licensing of banks, not the creation of the NBFC-MFI category.

question: Which force causes the trade winds of the southern hemisphere to start blowing from southwest to northeast in India after crossing the equator?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Coriolis force.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Coriolis force, arising from the Earth's rotation, deflects moving air (and water) to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere. (कोरिओलिस बल — पृथ्वी का घूर्णन)

 

• The southeast trade winds of the Southern Hemisphere, on crossing the equator during the Indian summer monsoon, get deflected by the Coriolis force and turn into southwest winds, giving India its southwest monsoon.

 

• The Coriolis force is zero at the equator and increases with latitude, acting perpendicular to the direction of wind motion, so it affects wind direction but not wind speed.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• This deflection phenomenon is also referred to as Ferrel's Law.

 

• The Coriolis force also influences ocean currents and the rotation of large-scale weather systems like cyclones.

 

NOTE

 

• Gravitational force (Option 1): Governs the weight/attraction of objects toward Earth's centre; not responsible for wind deflection.

 

• Magnetic force (Option 2): Relates to Earth's magnetic field and has no role in deflecting trade winds.

 

• Centrifugal force (Option 3): A pseudo-force acting outward due to rotation, distinct from the Coriolis effect that deflects wind direction.

question: Which of the following Indian states was NOT the host of FIFA Under-17 Women's World Cup Football 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup India 2022 was hosted across three venues: Bhubaneswar (Odisha), Goa (Panaji), and Navi Mumbai (Maharashtra). (फीफा अंडर-17 महिला विश्व कप 2022 — भारत)

 

• Punjab was not among the host states/venues for this tournament.

 

• The final was held at the DY Patil Stadium, Navi Mumbai, where Spain defeated Colombia to win the title.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's own team participated as the host nation in this edition, playing its group matches in Bhubaneswar.

 

• India had earlier hosted the (men's) FIFA U-17 World Cup in 2017, also across multiple venues.

 

NOTE

 

• Maharashtra (Option 1): Hosted matches at Navi Mumbai, including the final.

 

• Goa (Option 2): Hosted group and knockout matches of the tournament.

 

• Odisha (Option 4): Hosted matches at Bhubaneswar's Kalinga Stadium, including India's group games.

question: What was the HDI value of China in 2021?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 0.768.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As per the UNDP Human Development Report, China's Human Development Index (HDI) value for 2021 was 0.768, placing it in the "high human development" category. (मानव विकास सूचकांक — चीन 2021)

 

• The HDI is a composite index measuring average achievement in three basic dimensions: a long and healthy life, knowledge (education), and a decent standard of living.

 

• China's HDI ranked it around the 79th position globally in that report; India, for the same period, was classified under "medium human development" with a considerably lower value.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The HDI is published annually by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), with country values ranging from 0 to 1, higher values indicating higher development.

 

• Countries are grouped into four categories: Very High, High, Medium, and Low human development.

 

NOTE

 

• 0.645 (Option 2): Does not match China's officially reported 2021 HDI figure.

 

• 0.557 (Option 3): Does not match China's officially reported 2021 HDI figure.

 

• 0.750 (Option 4): Close to, but does not match, China's officially reported 2021 HDI figure of 0.768.

question: Which of these is NOT a characteristic of a free-enterprise economy?
option_1: Decisions are based on the forces of demand and supply.
option_2: Factor rewards are based on the productivity of factors of production.
option_3: All economic decisions are taken by the economic planners.
option_4: Economic decisions are regulated by the market.
solution_text:
The correct answer is All economic decisions are taken by the economic planners.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A free-enterprise (capitalist/market) economy is one where economic decisions — what to produce, how to produce, and for whom — are guided by market forces of demand and supply, with minimal government intervention. (मुक्त उद्यम अर्थव्यवस्था — बाजार आधारित निर्णय)

 

• In such an economy, factor rewards (wages, rent, interest, profit) are determined by the productivity/contribution of the factors of production, and prices are set by the market rather than by the state.

 

• Centralised decision-making, where "all economic decisions are taken by the economic planners", is instead the defining feature of a planned (socialist/command) economy, not a free-enterprise one.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Real-world economies are usually mixed economies, combining elements of both market mechanisms and government planning/regulation, as in India.

 

• Key features of a free-enterprise economy include private property rights, freedom of choice, profit motive, and competition.

 

NOTE

 

• Decisions based on demand and supply (Option 1): This IS a genuine characteristic of a free-enterprise economy, so it is not the answer.

 

• Factor rewards based on productivity (Option 2): This IS also a genuine characteristic of a free-enterprise economy, so it is not the answer.

 

• Economic decisions regulated by the market (Option 4): This too IS a characteristic of a free-enterprise economy, so it is not the answer.

question: Which regulatory body oversees microfinance institutions in India?
option_3: Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)
option_4: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
solution_text:
The correct answer is Reserve Bank of India (RBI).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is the principal regulator overseeing Non-Banking Financial Company - Microfinance Institutions (NBFC-MFIs) in India, prescribing norms for capital adequacy, interest rate caps, and lending practices. (भारतीय रिज़र्व बैंक — सूक्ष्म वित्त विनियमन)

 

• RBI's regulatory framework for microfinance was strengthened after the Malegam Committee (2011) recommendations and further harmonised in 2022 to bring all lenders (banks, NBFCs, and NBFC-MFIs) under a uniform regulatory regime for microfinance loans.

 

• Certain NGO-MFIs and cooperative-society-based MFIs may also be governed by state-level legislation, but the dominant regulator for NBFC-MFIs is the RBI.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• NABARD also plays a supportive/refinancing role for microfinance and rural credit, but is not the primary regulator.

 

• RBI additionally regulates banks, NBFCs, and payment systems in India under the RBI Act, 1934, and the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

 

NOTE

 

• Ministry of Finance (Option 2): The apex government body for economic/financial policy, but day-to-day regulation of microfinance institutions rests with the RBI.

 

• IRDAI (Option 3): Regulates the insurance sector in India, unrelated to microfinance institutions.

 

• SEBI (Option 4): Regulates the securities/capital markets, not microfinance institutions.

question: In which State of India is Sher Shah's Tomb located?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bihar.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sher Shah Suri's Tomb is located at Sasaram, in the Rohtas district of Bihar. (शेरशाह का मकबरा — सासाराम, बिहार)

 

• Built in red sandstone, it stands amid an artificial lake and is considered one of the finest examples of Indo-Afghan architecture, seen by many historians as a precursor to later Mughal mausoleum design.

 

• Sher Shah Suri founded the Sur Empire and is also credited with building the Grand Trunk (GT) Road and introducing the Rupiya currency.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Sher Shah Suri defeated Humayun to establish his rule over North India and introduced significant administrative reforms in the revenue and postal systems.

 

• The tomb was designed by architect Aliwal Khan and completed around 1545 CE, shortly after Sher Shah's death.

 

NOTE

 

• Uttar Pradesh (Option 2): Does not house Sher Shah's Tomb; the monument is located specifically in Bihar.

 

• Punjab (Option 3): Does not house Sher Shah's Tomb.

 

• Bengal (Option 4): Does not house Sher Shah's Tomb.

question: Which of the following associations was formed in Maharashtra to get social justice for the weaker sections of society?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Satya Shodhak Samaj.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Satya Shodhak Samaj ("Truth-Seekers' Society") was founded by Jyotirao Phule in 1873 in Pune, Maharashtra, to fight caste discrimination and secure social justice and equal rights for the lower castes, women, and other weaker sections of society. (सत्यशोधक समाज — ज्योतिराव फुले, महाराष्ट्र)

 

• The organisation campaigned against Brahmanical dominance and priesthood-based exploitation, promoted education for girls and the depressed classes, and conducted rituals without Brahmin priests.

 

• Phule and his wife Savitribai Phule also opened some of India's earliest schools for girls and for lower-caste children in Pune.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Satya Shodhak Samaj later influenced leaders like Shahu Maharaj of Kolhapur and contributed to the broader non-Brahmin movement in Maharashtra.

 

• Jyotirao Phule was posthumously given the title "Mahatma".

 

NOTE

 

• Theosophical Society (Option 1): Founded in 1875 in New York by Madame Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott, later headquartered at Adyar, Chennai; focused on spiritualism/comparative religion, not the Maharashtra weaker-sections movement.

 

• Arya Samaj (Option 2): Founded by Swami Dayananda Saraswati in 1875 in Bombay, focused on Vedic reform, but is chiefly associated with the reform movement in North India, not this Maharashtra-based social-justice association.

 

• Dharma Paripalana Yogam (Option 4): Founded by associates of Sree Narayana Guru in Kerala, not Maharashtra.

question: Identify the FALSE statement.
option_1: RBI decides the bank rate for the economy
option_2: SEBI conducts open market operations to regulate money supply in the economy
solution_text:
The correct answer is SEBI conducts open market operations to regulate money supply in the economy.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Open Market Operations (OMOs) — the buying and selling of government securities to regulate money supply and liquidity — are conducted by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), not by SEBI. (खुला बाजार परिचालन — RBI का कार्य, SEBI का नहीं)

 

• SEBI (Securities and Exchange Board of India) is the regulator of the securities/capital markets; it has no role in conducting OMOs or regulating overall money supply.

 

• The other three statements are factually correct: RBI decides the bank rate; RBI prints/issues currency notes (including ₹100 notes) under the RBI Act; and the Government of India/Ministry of Finance is responsible for coins, including the ₹1 coin.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Coins in India are minted under the authority of the Government of India as per the Coinage Act, while currency notes are issued by the RBI under Section 22 of the RBI Act, 1934.

 

• Other RBI monetary policy tools besides OMOs and the bank rate include the repo rate, reverse repo rate, CRR and SLR.

 

NOTE

 

• RBI decides the bank rate (Option 1): This is a TRUE statement — the bank rate is indeed fixed by the RBI — so it is not the false statement being sought.

 

• RBI prints the ₹100 currency notes (Option 3): This is also a TRUE statement, since currency notes are printed/issued under RBI's authority.

 

• Ministry of Finance issues ₹1 coins (Option 4): This is a TRUE statement too, as coins (including ₹1) are issued by the Government of India/Ministry of Finance, not the RBI.

question: Which of the following words was NOT a part of the original Preamble of the Indian Constitution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Secular.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The original Preamble (1950) described India as a "SOVEREIGN DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC". The words "Socialist" and "Secular" were NOT part of the original text. (पंथनिरपेक्ष शब्द — 42वां संविधान संशोधन, 1976)

 

• The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 (enacted during the Emergency, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee) inserted the words "Socialist" and "Secular", along with "Integrity" (making it "unity and integrity of the nation"), into the Preamble.

 

• After the 1976 amendment, the Preamble describes India as a "SOVEREIGN SOCIALIST SECULAR DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 42nd Amendment is often called the "Mini-Constitution" because of the sweeping changes it made.

 

• The Preamble has been amended only once, via the 42nd Amendment; the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973) had earlier held that the Preamble is part of the Constitution and can be amended, but not its "basic structure".

 

NOTE

 

• Democratic (Option 1): This word WAS part of the original 1950 Preamble.

 

• Republic (Option 2): This word WAS part of the original 1950 Preamble.

 

• Sovereign (Option 4): This word WAS part of the original 1950 Preamble.

question: Which of the following article says that 'It shall be the duty of every citizen of India who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 51A(k).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 51A(k) of the Indian Constitution casts a Fundamental Duty on every parent/guardian "to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years." (अनुच्छेद 51A(k) — शिक्षा का कर्तव्य)

 

• This duty was inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002, the same amendment that added Article 21A (Right to Education as a Fundamental Right) for children aged 6-14 years.

 

• Article 51A(k) is the eleventh and last of the Fundamental Duties listed in Part IVA of the Constitution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties were originally added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976 (on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee), with ten duties [51A(a) to (j)]; the 86th Amendment added the eleventh duty, 51A(k).

 

• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, i.e., they cannot be directly enforced by courts, unlike Fundamental Rights.

 

NOTE

 

• 51A(j) (Option 2): Relates to the duty to strive towards excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity.

 

• 51A(i) (Option 3): Relates to the duty to safeguard public property and abjure violence.

 

• 51A(h) (Option 4): Relates to the duty to develop the scientific temper, humanism and the spirit of inquiry and reform.

question: How much wage compensation per trainee is provided under the PM DAKSH Yojana?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rs. 3000.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The PM-DAKSH (Pradhan Mantri Dakshta Aur Kushalta Sampann Hitgrahi) Yojana, launched by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, is a skill-development scheme for marginalised groups such as SCs, OBCs, EWS, and Safai Karamcharis/waste-pickers. (पीएम दक्ष योजना — कौशल विकास एवं मजदूरी क्षतिपूर्ति)

 

• Under the scheme, eligible trainees are provided free skill training along with a wage compensation to offset loss of daily earnings during the training period, set at Rs. 3,000 per trainee.

 

• The scheme is implemented through national-level institutions such as NSFDC, NBCFDC, and NSKFDC, offering short-term and long-term skilling programmes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• PM-DAKSH offers courses under categories like Up-skilling/Re-skilling, Short Term Training Programme (STTP), Long Term Training Programme, and Entrepreneurship Development Programme (EDP).

 

• The scheme aims to enhance the employability and income-earning capacity of marginalised sections through market-oriented skill training.

 

NOTE

 

• Rs. 6000 (Option 2): Does not match the wage compensation amount specified under the PM-DAKSH Yojana.

 

• Rs. 8000 (Option 3): Does not match the wage compensation amount specified under the PM-DAKSH Yojana.

 

• Rs. 2000 (Option 4): Does not match the wage compensation amount specified under the PM-DAKSH Yojana.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are true regarding the Green Revolution?

i. The term 'green revolution' was coined by Sir William Gaud.

ii. Norman Borlaug is hailed as the Father of Green Revolution.

iii. MS Randhawa is called the Father of Green Revolution in India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only i and ii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Statements i and ii are correct, while statement iii is incorrect. (हरित क्रांति — नॉर्मन बोरलॉग, एम.एस. स्वामीनाथन)

 

• Statement i: The term "Green Revolution" was coined by William S. Gaud, an administrator of USAID, in a 1968 speech describing the dramatic rise in agricultural productivity.

 

• Statement ii: Norman Borlaug, the American agronomist who developed high-yielding, disease-resistant wheat varieties, is globally hailed as the "Father of the Green Revolution" and was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.

 

• Statement iii is false: It is M.S. Swaminathan, not M.S. Randhawa, who is called the "Father of the Green Revolution in India" for adapting Borlaug's high-yield wheat varieties to Indian conditions in the 1960s.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green Revolution in India began in the mid-1960s, initially concentrated in states like Punjab, Haryana, and western Uttar Pradesh, focusing on wheat and rice.

 

• M.S. Randhawa was a distinguished civil servant, horticulturist and writer known for his contributions to Indian agriculture and Chandigarh's development, but he is not the one titled "Father of the Green Revolution in India".

 

NOTE

 

• Only i and iii (Option 1): Incorrect because statement iii wrongly credits M.S. Randhawa instead of M.S. Swaminathan.

 

• Only ii (Option 3): Incorrect because it wrongly excludes the true statement i.

 

• Only iii (Option 4): Incorrect because statement iii itself is false, and this option excludes the two true statements i and ii.

question: Balkar Sidhu was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akdemi Award 2020 for his contribution to ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is folk dance of Punjab.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Balkar Sidhu was conferred the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for 2020 for his contribution to the folk dance of Punjab (Bhangra). (बलकार सिद्धू — पंजाब का लोक नृत्य, संगीत नाटक अकादमी पुरस्कार)

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for music, dance and drama, confers this award annually to recognise excellence and lifetime contribution in the performing arts, including folk and traditional dance forms.

 

• Balkar Sidhu has been a long-standing figure in popularising Punjab's folk dance traditions, notably Bhangra, on stage.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi also confers awards for classical dance forms such as Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, Kathakali and Sattriya.

 

• Punjab's major folk dances include Bhangra (men) and Giddha (women).

 

NOTE

 

• Manipuri (Option 2): A classical dance form associated with Manipur, not Balkar Sidhu's field of contribution.

 

• Chhau (Option 3): A semi-classical/folk martial dance form associated with West Bengal (Purulia), Odisha (Mayurbhanj) and Jharkhand (Seraikella), not Punjab.

 

• folk dance of Maharashtra (Option 4): Balkar Sidhu's recognised contribution is to Punjab's folk dance, not Maharashtra's.

question: In 1834, who proposed a law that states that the current induced by a change in flow opposes the effect producing the change?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Heinrich Friedrich Lenz.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Heinrich Friedrich Lenz, a Baltic German physicist, formulated Lenz's Law in 1834, which states that the direction of an induced current is always such that it opposes the change in magnetic flux that produced it. (लेंज़ का नियम — 1834)

 

• Lenz's Law is essentially a consequence of the law of conservation of energy applied to electromagnetic induction, and complements Faraday's Law of Electromagnetic Induction.

 

• It is commonly expressed through the negative sign in Faraday's Law formula: EMF = -N(dΦ/dt).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lenz's Law explains phenomena such as eddy current braking and the working of induction motors and generators.

 

• Michael Faraday discovered electromagnetic induction itself in 1831, three years before Lenz formulated his law about the direction of the induced current.

 

NOTE

 

• David Brewster (Option 1): Known for Brewster's Law/angle, relating to the polarisation of light, not electromagnetic induction.

 

• Henry Moseley (Option 2): Known for Moseley's Law, relating atomic number to X-ray frequency, unrelated to induced currents.

 

• Christian Johann Doppler (Option 3): Known for the Doppler Effect, describing the change in frequency of waves relative to an observer, not electromagnetic induction.

question:
Match the columns.

States

A) Jharkhand

B) Himachal Pradesh

C) Telangana

D) Punjab

Cultural festivals

I) Karma

II) Chaitraul

III) Lohri

IV) Bathukamma
solution_text:
The correct answer is A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct matching is: A) Jharkhand - I) Karma; B) Himachal Pradesh - II) Chaitraul; C) Telangana - IV) Bathukamma; D) Punjab - III) Lohri. (कर्मा-झारखंड, बथुकम्मा-तेलंगाना, लोहड़ी-पंजाब)

 

• Karma (Karam) festival is a major tribal harvest festival of Jharkhand (also celebrated in Chhattisgarh, Odisha and Bihar), worshipping the Karam tree/deity for prosperity.

 

• Chaitraul is a spring carnival celebrated in parts of Himachal Pradesh (notably Sirmaur district), marking the onset of the Chaitra month.

 

• Bathukamma is a floral festival of Telangana, celebrated by women with flower stacks over nine days during Navratri, while Lohri is the harvest/bonfire festival of Punjab, celebrated in mid-January.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable Jharkhand tribal festivals include Sarhul and Sohrai.

 

• Telangana's Bonalu festival is another important cultural celebration of the state, dedicated to Goddess Mahakali.

 

NOTE

 

• A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III (Option 1): Incorrectly pairs Jharkhand with Bathukamma and Telangana with Karma; these two festivals are swapped between Jharkhand and Telangana.

 

• A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II (Option 2): Incorrectly pairs Jharkhand with Lohri, Himachal Pradesh with Karma, and Punjab with Chaitraul.

 

• A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I (Option 3): Incorrectly pairs Jharkhand with Chaitraul, Himachal Pradesh with Bathukamma, Telangana with Lohri, and Punjab with Karma.
